scenes.script_line: The quality of your life is shaped by the stories you consistently live from. Some stories move you forward. Others quietly hold you back. Life-giving stories support who you're becoming, and the direction your life is moving in. They reflect what is true, not just what feels true. It helps to see the difference clearly. A draining story is usually fixed. It looks backward, it's built on fear, and it's often borrowed from someone else's voice. A life-giving story is open. It looks forward, it's built on evidence, and it sounds like you at your best.

scenes.script_line: And this is important. A life-giving story is not just positive thinking. Telling yourself "everything is perfect" doesn't last, because part of you knows it isn't true. A life-giving story lasts because it is true. Here's an example of how powerful a story can be. For years, many people believed that running a mile in under four minutes simply couldn't be done. Athletes came close, again and again, and stopped just short. The barrier wasn't only physical. It was a story. Then, in May 1954, Roger Bannister ran a mile in under four minutes. And just weeks later, someone else did it too. Nothing

close-up of running shoes hitting the track

scenes.script_line: The same thing happens in our own lives. Think of someone who has always believed, "I'm not a leader. That's for other people." So they stay quiet in meetings. They let others take the opportunities. And every time they hold back, the story feels a little more true. Then someone they respect says, "You see things others miss. We need your voice." At first, it doesn't match how they see themselves. They question it. They point to their limitations. But something begins to shift. They test it. They speak up once, then again. And as they start to trust the new story, their actions follow. Not bec

scenes.script_line: Notice the order. The story changed first. Then the actions. Then the results. That's the order this workshop follows too. That's the heart of this workshop. You're not going to pretend. You're going to find what's actually true about you, and learn to live from it. Some of the steps will feel easy. Others will ask more of you. Trust the order. Each step prepares you for the one that follows.

scenes.script_line: In the next ten steps, you'll move from an old story that keeps you stuck, to a new one that gives you life. Your facilitator will now help you reflect on the stories that have shaped you so far.
